★ Auction Feasibility Framework: Exclusion of Star Retentions & Ineligible Profiles

A fatal flaw in naive sports analytics is ranking players purely by raw prestige or overall stats without evaluating auction feasibility. To ensure actionable utility for Rajasthan Royals in the IPL 2027 Auction, our recruitment engine enforces four non-negotiable operational filters:

1. Exclusion of Franchise Mega-Stars & Retained Faces

Players such as Virat Kohli, Jasprit Bumrah, Rohit Sharma, Suryakumar Yadav, Heinrich Klaasen, Shubman Gill, Rishabh Pant, and Sanju Samson command locked multi-year franchise retention contracts at maximum purse brackets (₹18–25+ Cr) or Right-To-Match (RTM) guarantees. It is statistically and commercially impossible for these players to enter the open auction pool for Rajasthan Royals in 2027. Recommending them wastes analytical bandwidth and provides zero actionable recruitment strategy.

2. Exclusion of Legally Ineligible Nationals

By BCCI regulatory policy and IPL governance protocols, Pakistani cricketers (e.g., Babar Azam, Mohammad Rizwan, Shaheen Afridi) are barred from registering for the IPL auction. All Pakistani players have been strictly removed from candidate pools to preserve legal compliance.

3. Exclusion of Top-Order Openers (Batting Positions 1–3)

Rajasthan Royals have already solidified their long-term opening partnership in Yashasvi Jaiswal and Vaibhav Sooryavanshi. Allocating auction capital to top-order anchors would cause roster redundancy. Our batting evaluation strictly isolates Middle-Order Enforcers & Death Finishers (Positions 4, 5, 6, 7).

4. Exclusion of Powerplay Opening Bowlers (>25% PP Overs)

RR's new-ball seam attack is already anchored by Jofra Archer, Sandeep Sharma, and Nandre Burger. The war room's urgent tactical requirement is Middle-Overs Spin Squeeze (Overs 7–15) and Death-Overs Yorker Lockdown (Overs 16–20). Bowlers bowling over 25% of their deliveries in the powerplay were filtered out.

1 What Counts as Pressure? The Pre-Delivery Mathematical Framework

Cricket analytics often errs by defining pressure simply as "the death overs". In reality, a team needing 85 off 12 balls with 9 wickets down is in the 19th over, but the contest is dead (zero leverage). Conversely, 30/3 in over 5 generates immense stress.

Our analytical framework evaluates pressure strictly on the pre-delivery match state across all 200,999 balls (IPL and T20I, 2022–2026), preventing outcome leakage:

2nd Innings (Chasing Context)

  • Required Run Rate Stress 35% Weight: Measures scoring acceleration required relative to contemporary T20 par rates (scaled from 6.0 to 18.0+ RPO).
  • Wickets in Hand 30% Weight: Quantifies exponential resource depletion as wickets fall (0 to 10 wickets down).
  • Innings Urgency 20% Weight: Compounding time penalty as remaining deliveries tick down (0 to 120 balls).
  • Win Probability Leverage Index 15% Weight: Mathematical swing potential, peaking in 50-50 high-stakes situations [Formula: 4 × WP × (1 - WP)].

1st Innings (Target Setting Context)

  • Phase Leverage 40% Weight: Overs 16–20 carry maximum scoring variance and match-winning swing potential.
  • Collapse Recovery 35% Weight: Evaluates performance when batting under top-order collapse (excess wickets lost vs expected).
  • Par Deficit Pressure 25% Weight: Urgency created when the team runs behind the 8.50 RPO baseline par total.
  • Tournament Stakes: 1.15× multiplier applied for knockout, playoff, and final fixtures.

2 Top 10 Batters Under Pressure: Clutch Batting Index (CBI)
